title: VastPipe: A High-Throughput Inference System via Adaptive Space-Division Multiplexing for Diverse Accelerators
authors: Li-Xian Ma and Le-Ping Wang and En Shao and Rong-Yu Cao and Guang-Ming Tan
venue: Journal of Computer Science and Technology
mechanism: MPS adaptive quotas; separate AMD CU-mask stratum
environment: Local NVIDIA A100: TensorRT serving, MPS; AMD MI100: TVM/ROCm with hipExtStreamCreateWithCUMask. GPU memory, OS, driver and runtime versions NOT EXTRACTED for these GPU experiments. NPU Table3 is not the GPU configuration.
workload: Co-located CV pairs (VGG16/GoogLeNet, VGG19/GoogLeNet, ResNet101/InceptionV3, VGG19/ResNet50); NLP/CV pairs with BERT/GPT2; Poisson-generated request mixes. Exact GPU batch sizes and rates NOT EXTRACTED.
comparator: No MPS; default MPS without per-service quotas; RL-selected MPS quotas. AMD no/default CU mask separately.
finding: A100 VGG16+GoogLeNet: throughput 2.7x no MPS and 1.5x default MPS; not a universal average or p99 result. NLP/CV mean 2.43x no MPS, 1.45x default MPS. MI100 mean 1.89x no mask, 1.24x default mask.
limitation: Include only local GPU inference evidence, not the main 1000-NPU cluster results. Offline Q-table assumes relatively stable request mix; GPU-specific quotas, repetitions and variance unresolved. Chart bars are not preserved in Markdown. title: ArkGPU: enabling applications' high-goodput co-location execution on multitasking GPUs
authors: Jie Lou and Yiming Sun and Jie Zhang and Huawei Cao and Yuan Zhang and Ninghui Sun
venue: CCF Transactions on High Performance Computing
mechanism: CUDA API interception + NVML monitoring and admission throttling
environment: Machine with four V100s; Xeon Platinum8163; CentOS7.9.2009; driver460.106.00; CUDA11.1; cuDNN7.6.5. Per-GPU memory/framework versions NOT EXTRACTED.
workload: Five MLPerf inference LC models (ResNet50, SSD-MobileNet, SSD-ResNet34, DLRM, BERT), each paired locally with six BE training models (30 pairs). Single-stream query size1; p99 QoS threshold twice solo. Separate four-GPU app-mixes are not local occupancy evidence.
comparator: MPS (Non-ArkGPU); k8s-native for QPS/utilization; GaiaGPU and adjustment-unit ablation. MPS quota settings NOT EXTRACTED.
finding: Section5.2 reports all30 tested pairs satisfy the 2x-solo p99 QoS target with ArkGPU. Low-contention pairs can lose about5% QPS from throttling. Four-GPU app-mix goodput gains94.98% vs k8s-native and38.65% vs MPS are separate system-level results.
limitation: Mixed inference/training qualifies via explicit inference p99/QPS and workload transfer rationale; it does not establish inference-only performance. Polling/API sleeps can add delay; BE checkpoint/restart affects costs. Huge goodput ratios can have near-zero baseline yield. Repetitions/variance and chart coordinates unresolved.

title: Dyna-P: placement-aware dynamic partitioning for lightweight applications with modern GPUs
mechanism: MIG dynamic placement/reconfiguration with reconfiguration-last policy
environment: Two A30s,24GB each; CUDA12.2; driver535.171.04; DCGM3.1.3. Local sections4.2/4.3.1 use one A30. StaCon profiles2g.12gb+1g.6gb+1g.6gb. OS/backend versions NOT EXTRACTED.
workload: 50 SLM inference jobs; batch1-64; DistilGPT, Codegen, Flan-T5-Large, Codellama and Phi-1 as labelled in Table2. Local batch sensitivity:10 inference jobs, batches1-8 vs32-64 on one A30. Later160-A100 cluster study is simulation.
comparator: Full-GPU sequential baseline; fixed StaCon MIG; pre-profiled MISO adapted to A30; ORACLE with future job/size/time knowledge.
finding: Single-A30 batch experiments: smaller partitions increase concurrency but can increase mean JCT; not online p99 evidence. Fig8 broader job set reports39.03% lower makespan vs StaCon,12.14% vs MISO and14.7% higher normalized STP vs StaCon. Prediction-error sensitivity:15% perturbation adds8.09% makespan.
limitation: Retain one-GPU inference strata separately from two-GPU aggregate and cluster simulation. JCT/makespan/STP cannot replace request-tail latency or goodput. Reconfiguration can stop/restart active jobs; neither architectural MIG claims nor OOM avoidance prove hostile isolation. Model labels/parameter counts and corrupted overhead fraction require caution.

title: iGniter: Interference-Aware GPU Resource Provisioning for Predictable DNN Inference in the Cloud
authors: Fei Xu and Jianian Xu and Jiabin Chen and Li Chen and Ruitao Shang and Zhi Zhou and Fangming Liu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
mechanism: MPS active-thread quotas + interference-aware batch/provisioning and shadow process
environment: Ten EC2 p3.2xlarge instances,one V100 each,8vCPU/61GB; Triton2.12.0,TensorRT8.0.1.6. MPS active-thread percentage; allocation unit2.5%. Heterogeneous extension adds20 T4 instances. OS/driver/CUDA version NOT EXTRACTED.
workload: AlexNet,ResNet50,VGG19(ImageNet),SSD(VOC2012);12 workload/SLO configurations; constant arrivals. Local experiment co-locates four models at25% quota,batch3. p99 provisioning measured over windows e.g.30s; model-validation experiments repeated3 times with SD bars.
comparator: FFD+; GSLICE+ with iGniter placement; gpu-lets+ modified batch strategy and best-fit placement. These are adapted baselines.
finding: Local four-model latency prediction error1.53%-5.02%(Fig13). Fig14 deployment: iGniter6 GPUs/0 SLO violations vs gpu-lets+8/3,FFD+5/10,GSLICE+6/3;25% lower hourly instance cost vs gpu-lets+, not25% higher local utilization. Fig17 shows an initial p99 violation before shadow-process recovery.
limitation: Constant arrivals and four vision models limit bursty/LLM transfer. Negligible PCIe contention assumption can underpredict AlexNet; baselines modified. Steady-state/post-correction SLO success is not an unconditional guarantee; shadow standby incurs capacity/memory costs. Chart bars/latency traces unavailable in Markdown.

title: Real-time, Work-conserving GPU Scheduling for Concurrent DNN Inference
authors: Mingcong Han and Rong Chen and Weihang Shen and Hanze Zhang and Jinrong Yang and Haibo Chen
mechanism: Reset-based temporal preemption + dynamic kernel padding; NVIDIA binary instrumentation
environment: One MI50,16GB/60CUs;i7-10700,32GB RAM;Ubuntu20.04,ROCm4.3.0,TVM0.14.0. Separate one GV100,32GB/80SMs;CUDA11.4,PyTorch1.12.0,TensorRT8.5.1. Driver version NOT EXTRACTED.
workload: DISB A-E,uniform RT except Poisson E; closed-loop BE; ResNet152,VGG19,YOLOv3,BERT-base,GPT2 (128 tokens,GPT2 prefill). RT rates50%,100% or10% solo-throughput according to workload; Apollo/SVL trace. Separate LLM case batch1,100 decode tokens,MLC-LLM.
comparator: RT-only; sequential priority; GPU streams. NVIDIA closed-source strata compare priority-enabled Triton/TensorRT and Orion/PyTorch without dynamic padding.
finding: GV100 PyTorch DISB-C: Orion p99 normalized latency1.17x vs Reef below1.05x; normalized total throughput0.97x vs1.14x(Fig29). TensorRT comparison trades throughput: mean1.21x Triton vs1.11x Reef(Fig28). All ratios retain model-solo normalization; do not mix engines/AMD strata.
